question.text: A disclosed quantity (DQ) order in the derivatives segment allows a trader to:

answer.text: Show only a part of the total order quantity to the market, with the remaining hidden
Disclose the order to only selected trading members
Place an order that is visible only after a specific time
Place orders that bypass the normal matching algorithm

explanation.text: The Logic: A disclosed quantity (DQ) order allows the trader to display only a portion of the total order quantity in the market while the remaining quantity stays hidden. For example, if a trader wants to buy 10,000 contracts but shows only 2,000, the remaining 8,000 are not visible in the order book. As the displayed portion gets filled, the next tranche is automatically released. DQ orders are used by institutional participants to reduce the market-impact signal of large orders. The Trap: DQ orders do not pick selective counterparties, are not time-released to specific windows, and do not bypass the exchange's price-time matching algorithm - the disclosed portion follows normal price-time priority, and the hidden tranche only acquires fresh time priority when it becomes visible. Note: The specific disclosed-quantity order type and its hidden-remainder behavior are not described in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook, which on the pages checked covers day, IOC, limit, market and stop-loss orders, price-time matching, bid-ask spread and impact cost. The framing above is general Indian exchange order-type knowledge.
